correctness.rationale: Summing the causal geometric series on 0≤x<1 gives a uniformly bounded Zak extension to its closed one-sided cell; an edge zero lowers the essential infimum because the open cell approaches it through sets of positive measure. The numerator is U-rzV with U=1+c exp(-iθx), V=exp(-iθ)+c exp(-iθx); U and V cannot vanish together. The unit-circle criterion is Q=q(1+c²)+2cF=0, with F=Re[(1-r² exp(iθ)) exp(-iφ)], φ=θx. Q(0)>0. For θ≤π, F decreases to F(θ); requiring its minimum to be ≤−q gives r≥cos(θ/2). For θ>π, its unique minimum −|1-r² exp(iθ)| is interior (the displacement of the cosine places the minimum before the edge, where F′(θ)>0). The quadratic roots from these minima are positive reciprocal endpoints, including the singleton at onset; at h=1/2 they are (1±r)/(1∓r). The initial rising branch in the long regime is already above the target level; after the minimum a second open-cell intersection occurs precisely for Q(θ)>0, or an edge zero at equality. Tangency at the two long-regime amplitude endpoints and the short-regime one-sided edge behavior follow from the same geometry. The claimed conservative frame bound uses r^x≥r and the upper denominator bounds; inverse Fourier transformation gives the stated two distinct equally elevated Cauchy poles.
